parts.name: Titanium frame
parts.description: Light, but expensive, and carries less than steel.

parts.name: Solid aluminium wheels
parts.description: Cheap and heavy. Lower grip in soft regolith.

parts.name: Wire-mesh wheels
parts.description: Light, fast and grippy, like the Apollo rover's. Bulky.

parts.name: Fixed solar panel
parts.description: A flat panel. Catches little of a low Sun.

parts.name: Vertical solar mast
parts.description: Faces the low polar Sun. Light, expensive and bulky.

parts.name: Nickel-hydrogen battery
parts.description: Proven and cheap. Stores the most, but heavy.

parts.name: Lithium-ion battery
parts.description: Light, but expensive and stores less.

parts.name: LED floodlights
parts.description: Lets the rover see inside shadowed craters.

parts.name: Radioisotope heater units
parts.description: Steady heat from decaying isotopes. Slows freezing in the cold.

parts.name: Regolith drill
parts.description: Samples the soil, and ice where it exists. Heavier and bulkier than the camera.

parts.name: Neutron spectrometer
parts.description: Senses hydrogen in the top meter of soil while the rover drives, as on NASA's VIPER. A live meter that draws energy while switched on.

parts.name: X-ray spectrometer
parts.description: Reads a rock's main elements: park beside a boulder and hold still.

parts.name: Seismometer station
parts.description: Set it down on the ground before the moonquake to record it. Its mass leaves the rover.

parts.name: Laser retroreflector
parts.description: Mirrors for lasers fired from Earth. Needs no power; set it down where Earth is in view. Its mass leaves the rover.
